chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Umrah is obligatory upon the creation, in the status of Hajj upon the one who has the ability for it, because Allah the Exalted says: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah', and indeed the Umrah was revealed at Al-Medina.
I said to him, 'So the one who enjoys (Tamattu) with the Umrah to the Hajj, would that suffice from him?' He said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: Is Umrah obligatory for Muslims and how does it relate to Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes Umrah as an individual obligation (wajib) for those with capacity, equating its status to Hajj based on the verse 'And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah.' The scholar notes the specific context of its revelation in Medina and confirms that the Tamattu' mode—performing Umrah first and then Hajj—fully satisfies the obligation, reflecting the Ja'fari jurisprudence view on the unity of these rites.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Umra is Obligatory upon the people at the status of the Hajj upon the one who has the ability for it, because Allahazwj the Exalted is Saying [2:196] And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah, and rather the Umra was Revealed at Al-Medina’.
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So the one who enjoys (Tamattu) with the Umra to the Hajj, would that suffice from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

‘Al-’Umrah is obligatory on the creatures as al-Hajj is if they are able to perform; Allah, most High, has said, ‘Complete al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah for the sake of Allah.’ [2:196] Al-’Umrah came in al-Madinah.’
I then asked, ‘Those who benefit (al-Tamattu‘) in al-‘Umrah and al-Hajj’, is that kind sufficient?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient.’”
